correctness.rationale: Evenness and the differentiated remainder make f′δ(y)/y strictly increasing as a function of y² in a sufficiently small chart, with its two nonzero zeros at y=±yδ and yδ²=Aδ/(2B)+O(δ²). The unique base left support gives a positive horizontal gap on the compact exterior of the chart. On the retained arcs f″δ>0 locally, and exterior curvature stays positive. The common vertical supporting chord lies outside the discarded arc; the simple closed splice has matching tangents and nonnegative turning, hence bounds the hull. Indeed the original is enclosed by the splice and the splice consists of retained points and convex combinations of the two endpoints. For δ<0 the curvature remains positive. With Y²=A/(2B) the cap integrals give coefficients 2B∫₀^Y(z²−Y²)² dz=16BY⁵/15 and 16B²∫₀^Y z²(z²−Y²)² dz=128B²Y⁷/105. Their ratio is 4A/7 after removing the extra δ. For analytic families the nonzero stationary condition is an analytic equation in y² and δ, and scaling the integrals to a fixed interval makes the two defects δ^(5/2) and δ^(7/2) times nonvanishing analytic factors, with zero negative-side extensions. For the limaçon the supporting line is obtained by minimizing c+qc²; the retained arc has curvature numerator at least 2q²−1/2>0. The omitted upper arc has y′=cos t−q cos(2t)>0 (its minimum in c=cos t occurs at an endpoint); integrating the area by parts gives 2∫(1−q cos t)sin²t(2q cos t−1)dt from 0 to t_q, which reduces to the displayed expression. The speed gives the asserted perimeter formula. Inverting y=(1−q cos t)sin t yields A=4 and B=2 and both quoted constants. Frozen quadrature and script evidence is supplementary and was inspected, not executed.
